execution.1: No verifiable deployment or qualification artifact.
execution.3: Real product and customers, but counts are self-reported or undated.
execution.5: Named programme, dated, with qualification artifacts and third-party or filing-grade disclosure.

access.1: No evidenced route to an Indian CV buyer.
access.3: One evidenced channel or partnership, no named end customer.
access.5: Multiple evidenced routes including OEM line-fit or standing tender position.

leverage.1: Owns nothing DeepGrid must pass through.
leverage.3: Owns IP or a channel that raises DeepGrid's cost but can be routed around.
leverage.5: Owns a control point DeepGrid cannot bypass — the safety case, the platform slot, or the certification.

competitors.name: ZF CVCS India
competitors.why_e: Named Indian E-Mobility CV OEM nomination with 16 features; 300,000 km India validation; ARAI certification claimed; a listed ₹29,642 Cr entity.
competitors.why_a: OEM line-fit nomination plus its own Indian homologation capability and an export business to ~18 countries.
competitors.why_l: Owns the brake actuator, therefore owns the safety case. DeepGrid's perception output cannot reach AEBS without passing through an actuator owner.
competitors.conf_note: Nomination and feature scope primary; validation km and ARAI certification vendor-published, certificate numbers not released.

Government / PSU: Homologation capability, no evidenced tender position

competitors.blocker_why: Owns a DIFFERENT control point. DeepGrid intends to sell INTO an actuator owner, so ZF is the route rather than the obstacle — until it bundles perception itself.

competitors.name: Aptiv (+STRADVISION)
competitors.why_e: Indian CV OEM selected Gen 6 across 14 models and 30+ variants; 40m+ vehicles globally on the ADAS software.
competitors.why_a: 2,500 India engineers, 7 plants, 4 technical centres — but this is its FIRST Indian CV OEM ADAS collaboration, so India CV access is new.
competitors.why_l: Owns OEM platform selection and the OTA lifecycle. Once shipped, it improves the fleet after SOP and keeps the customer relationship.
competitors.conf_note: All load-bearing facts from a primary dated press release.

OEM / Tier-1: Named CV OEM platform win, 14 models

competitors.blocker_why: Decides who gets the seat. It selects the perception vendor for its camera and controls the OTA lifecycle afterwards — gatekeeper and prospective customer at once.

competitors.name: STRADVISION
competitors.why_e: ~5 million cumulative SVNet units and ISO 26262; the India CV lineup selection is dated April 2026 and therefore new.
competitors.why_a: Reaches OEMs THROUGH integrators — its India CV position is inside Aptiv's camera. No independent Indian channel evidenced.
competitors.why_l: Occupies the exact slot DeepGrid is bidding for — bounded perception, priced for constrained hardware, inside an accountable integrator — and holds the ISO 26262 DeepGrid lacks.
competitors.conf_note: Primary dated release; ISO 26262 vendor-published but specific.

OEM / Tier-1: Embedded in the winning Gen 6 stack

competitors.blocker_why: Occupies the seat. A bounded perception layer priced for constrained hardware, already inside the winning stack, holding the ISO 26262 DeepGrid lacks. Displacing it is the entire job.

competitors.name: drivebuddyAI
competitors.why_e: $5.3m across 3,600 e-buses and trucks, June 2026, disclosed by a listed parent, and won after an evaluation of competing solutions in live fleet operations.
competitors.why_a: Proven routes into public transport, seaport logistics, mining and industrial fleets — the arenas the dossier nominates for DeepGrid's fastest proof.
competitors.why_l: Camera-only with no AEB, so it owns nothing on the mandate path. Its real leverage is the parent's insurance flywheel, which DeepGrid cannot copy.
competitors.conf_note: Contract values from listed-parent disclosure; capability read from the same release.

Fleet / mining: Contracted, dated, and crossing into mining

competitors.blocker_why: Camera-only, no actuation. Owns retrofit share DeepGrid was never going to win on certification.

competitors.name: Sterling Tools × MINIEYE
competitors.why_e: Partnership exchange-filed and corroborated ×4, but no named Indian OEM nomination — the falsifier stands unfired.
competitors.why_a: A listed Indian component major with existing OEM relationships and manufacturing scale.
competitors.why_l: Holds the local manufacturing, channel and compliance role — the same role DeepGrid needs an integrator to play for it.
competitors.conf_note: Partnership verified; commercial outcome not evidenced.

OEM / Tier-1: Existing fastener relationships, no ADAS nomination

competitors.blocker_why: A partner-shaped competitor. Holds the local role DeepGrid needs someone to play, not the seat.

competitors.name: Starkenn
competitors.why_e: DOWNGRADED. The deployment count cannot be stated — one source gives 2,500, 700 and 300+ for the same quantity. Turnover ₹5 Cr, 57 staff and shrinking 15.8% YoY on $2.0m lifetime funding.
competitors.why_a: HELD. 30% of revenue from government tenders plus DPIIT recognition is a standing empanelment position, and empanelment — not certification — is the gate in that arena.
competitors.why_l: No certification, no silicon, warning-only. Owns nothing DeepGrid must pass through.
competitors.conf_note: Access figure is self-reported and ~21 months old but directionally corroborated by the subscription model; execution evidence fails its own source.
competitors.blocker_why: Warning-only, uncertified. Blocks nothing on the perception-into-integrator path; competes for a different budget.

competitors.name: bitsensing
competitors.why_e: $42m raised across 5 rounds and a shipping India retrofit kit, but no India deployment volume established.
competitors.why_a: One evidenced Indian channel (IKIO MoU); no named end customer.
competitors.why_l: NXP partnership and real radar IP, but warning-only caps it below the mandate line at any price.
competitors.conf_note: Funding and partnership dated and corroborated; India traction not established.

Fleet / mining: Retrofit kit is real, volume unknown

competitors.blocker_why: Radar retrofit with a hard warning-only ceiling; no overlap with the perception seat.

competitors.name: Netrasemi
competitors.why_e: A2000 production-ready May 2026 with trials under way; commercial mid-2027.
competitors.why_a: Surveillance and automotive trials, no named CV customer.
competitors.why_l: Indian edge-AI silicon weakens 'India-native' as a DeepGrid differentiator, but carries no AIS, AEC-Q100 or ISO 26262.
competitors.conf_note: National business daily, dated; Series A not re-verified against a primary filing.
competitors.blocker_why: Erodes 'India-native' as a differentiator without competing for the seat; its mid-2027 window is when that changes.

competitors.name: Gahan AI
competitors.why_e: No dated primary artifact for any capability claim. 15 employees. The one peer-reviewed output is a simulation platform.
competitors.why_a: Claimed Tata and Ather pilots are self-published; no corroboration from either counterparty.
competitors.why_l: Lowered 2->1 on external challenge: the leverage scale defines 1 as 'owns nothing DeepGrid must pass through', and TI does not corroborate the exclusivity while AEC-Q100 attaches to TI's IC rather than to Gahan's platform. No chokepoint is evidenced.
competitors.conf_note: Every capability claim self-published and undated; the absence is measured, not assumed.
competitors.blocker_why: Competes for the same indigenous-perception narrative and the same government sympathy, on claims no third party has corroborated.
